findings.claim: NewGrandchild always skips when /bin/sh, /bin/sleep or /bin/ps is missing, even when CI is "true". L86 says these tests skip locally and fail on CI without their tools, as overlaytest.RequireShAndAwk does (overlaytest.go:67-70). The helper's unconditional t.Skipf breaks that. On a CI image without /bin/ps, which is common in minimal containers and busybox images, X1, E1 (t) and SH15 all skip and pass. Those three tests are the only regression checks for 4b9c3789c2e0-3 F1 and -5 F1, so the fixed WARNING can come back with green CI. Today's ubuntu runners have /bin/ps, so this is not triggered yet.

Setpgid moves sh out of the hook's process group. Only labdrian's own context deadline now kills the run. If the hook process is killed from outside before its 2 s deadline (SIGKILL or a signal sent to the hook's group, for example by Claude Code's own hook timeout), Cancel never runs. The run's group then survives as an orphan. The stuck-awk case that motivated this change would then run with no limit, where before a kill sent to the hook's group would have reached it. L86 accepted this tradeoff without verifying how Claude Code stops a hook. No test covers it, and the README and CHANGELOG do not mention it.

Cancel sends syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, SIGKILL) by raw pid. It skips os.Process.Kill, which tracks whether the process was already waited for and uses a pidfd on Linux. exec.Cmd can call Cancel from its context goroutine while Wait reaps the process at the same moment; X3 tests Cancel after Run has fully returned. If the deadline expires just as the group's last process exits and is reaped, and the pid is reused as the pgid of an unrelated new group, that group gets SIGKILL. The window is very small, but the kill is a SIGKILL to processes this code does not own.

X1 (and E1 (t) at engine/review/evidencesh/evidencesh_unix_test.go:21) gives the stub 200 ms, then calls g.Started, which fails when the pid file is missing. On a loaded machine (`go test ./...` running packages in parallel), the group kill can land before the subshell writes `$!`, or while it is writing it; an empty file fails pid()'s Atoi. Both tests then fail even though the code is correct. This also contradicts RequireGone's doc (grandchild_unix.go:86), which treats a grandchild that never started as gone, a case Started always turns into a failure.

The doc says that on a build that is not Unix "a process it forked can outlive the call, up to killGrace". That is wrong: killGrace limits how long the call waits for the pipes (WaitDelay), not how long the forked process lives. A grandchild that is never killed outlives the call for as long as it runs. A reader who trusts the comment would think non-Unix builds leave no orphans after 2 s.
